facts.heading: Anxiety worsens in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and it gets worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.

facts.heading: Deputy head role
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school. She has taught at the school for 11 years.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school. I've taught here for 11 years

facts.heading: Asked to step up
facts.content: Hannah was asked to step up when the deputy left.
facts.evidence: and then had asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person. And that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Nighttime anxiety symptoms
facts.content: Mostly on Sunday evenings, Hannah's chest tightens and she rehearses meetings in her head.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing potential questions
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say and how she would be perceived.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say then what they would think of me if I got it wrong

facts.heading: Fear of incompetence
facts.content: Hannah fears that people will think she is incapable of reading.
facts.evidence: That time out of my depth that they gave the job to a nice ear for teacher who can't actually read

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the same email to the governor's four times. The email was about the behavior policy.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governor's four times. Uh, changed to the behavior policy.

facts.heading: Fear of appearing stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Governor's reaction
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves treated Hannah kindly and was delighted when he talked to her in September.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind. He talked me in September. He was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling of lying
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about her capability.
facts.evidence: that makes it worse somehow because I feel like I'm lying to him. About being capable as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Comparing to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares her current job to her mother's career. She thinks her mother would have done things better.
facts.evidence: Everything they do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's support statement
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has always worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Mother's statement effect
facts.content: When her mother says this, Hannah feels like she is making a fuss to avoid telling her how bad it is.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking late every morning
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning going through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine. Then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking pattern started recently
facts.content: Hannah has been waking like this since the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term.

facts.heading: Drinks many cups of coffee
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Exhausted from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day from pretending.
facts.evidence: I'm exhausted by the end of every day. just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's advice
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben suggested she should just enjoy the situation.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feeling guilty and alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben gives advice.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's profession
facts.content: Ben is an engineer.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer.

facts.heading: Partner's view on problems
facts.content: Ben thinks if something is a problem, Hannah should fix it.
facts.evidence: He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it.

facts.heading: Difficulty seeking support
facts.content: Hannah does not have friends who talk to her anymore.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really.

facts.heading: Lost social group due to role
facts.content: Hannah lost friends because she became their line manager.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and they talk for it.

facts.heading: Lost company with promotion
facts.content: Hannah lost some company along with a promotion.
facts.evidence: So you lost some company along with the promotion? Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that.

facts.heading: Misses the children most
facts.content: Hannah misses the children the most.
facts.evidence: The children mostly.

facts.heading: Current life is spreadsheets
facts.content: Hannah's current days are filled with spreadsheets.
facts.evidence: Now my days are spreadsheets.

facts.heading: Desire for deeper meaning
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted a deeper meaning.
facts.evidence: I thought I did.

facts.heading: Refusal to say no
facts.content: Hannah sat yes in the room because she could not say no to her.
facts.evidence: I sat yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Crying after a confrontation
facts.content: Hannah went home and cried after an interaction.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Thought about not returning
facts.content: Hannah thought that she would never get to go back.
facts.evidence: I think and that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during summer holidays in the lakes.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays we went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for 10 days.

facts.heading: Difference during holiday
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of Hannah.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me.

facts.heading: Holiday behavior
facts.content: During the holiday, Hannah was just talking and carrying sandwiches.
facts.evidence: I was just talking, but carried the sandwiches.

facts.heading: Return to stress before term
facts.content: The week before term, Hannah was a wreck again.
facts.evidence: The week before the term I was a wreck again.

facts.heading: Inability to eat sundae
facts.content: Hannah could not eat on the sundae before term.
facts.evidence: I couldn't eat on the sundae.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down good things each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening, small things, a trail of laughing, a good email. It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Stopped writing due to feeling silly
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing because she felt silly about it. She felt like she was bragging to herself.
facts.evidence: I stopped because I felt silly. As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook.

facts.heading: Wants to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Wants to avoid rehearsing meetings
facts.content: Hannah wants to walk into a meeting without rehearsing it first.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first.

facts.heading: Wants to send emails once
facts.content: Hannah wants to send an email only once.
facts.evidence: Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Wants to feel less anxious at night
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa without her stomach in knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feelings about stating goals
facts.content: Hannah felt light and a bit tearful when talking about her goals.
facts.evidence: Lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful actually.

facts.heading: First time telling someone bad news
facts.content: This is the first time Hannah has told anyone about something bad.
facts.evidence: That's the first time I have told anyone who bad it is.

facts.heading: Scared about telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah feels scared about telling Ben about something. She worries he would hear she didn't say sooner.
facts.evidence: Scary. He would probably be heard that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Prefers quiet moment to share

facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too warmed up.

facts.heading: Suggests Saturday morning for sharing
facts.content: Hannah suggested Saturday morning as a time to share.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? Yeah, over breakfast. He's always in a good mood then.
